searchDocs.title: Disconnect​
searchDocs.content: </> type Disconnect = () → () Every listener method returns a Disconnect, the cleanup function. Call it to stop listening. It's safe to call more than once, and can be handed to a cleanup library or returned from a React effect.

searchDocs.title: version​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> ObservableValue.version: number Increases each time the value changes. It identifies a value even when a table was changed in place, which makes it a useful dependency for caches, or for React's useMemo / useEffect.

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> ObservableValue.new(initialValue: T) → ObservableValue<T> Creates an ObservableValue holding initialValue.

searchDocs.title: get​
searchDocs.content: </> ObservableValue:get() → T Returns the current value.

searchDocs.title: set​
searchDocs.content: </> ObservableValue:set(newValue: T) → () Sets the value. ObservableValue:onChanged fires if the value changed, and ObservableValue:onSet fires on every call. INFO Setting a table always fires onChanged, even if it's the same table, so a table you edited in place still notifies listeners when you set it.

searchDocs.title: update​
searchDocs.content: </> ObservableValue:update(update: (T) → T) → T Sets the value to update(currentValue) and returns the new value. health:update(function(current) return current - 10 end)

searchDocs.title: onChanged​
searchDocs.content: </> ObservableValue:onChanged(callback: ( newValue: T, oldValue: T ) → ()) → Disconnect Calls callback whenever the value changes.

searchDocs.title: onSet​
searchDocs.content: </> ObservableValue:onSet(callback: (newValue: T) → ()) → Disconnect Calls callback on every ObservableValue:set, including ones that don't change the value.

searchDocs.title: promiseValue​
searchDocs.content: </> ObservableValue:promiseValue(predicate: (T) → ( boolean, R )) → TypedPromise<R> Returns a promise that resolves with R the first time predicate(value) returns true, checking the current value first. If predicate errors, the promise rejects with that error. Cancelling the promise stops listening. local loaded = ObservableValue.new(false) loaded:promiseValue(function(isLoaded) return isLoaded, nil end):expect() -- yields until loaded is true

searchDocs.title: observe​
searchDocs.content: </> ObservableValue:observe(callback: ( newValue: T, oldValue: T? ) → ()) → Disconnect Calls callback straight away with the current value (oldValue is nil), then on every change.

searchDocs.title: Destroy​
searchDocs.content: </> ObservableValue:Destroy() → () Disconnects every listener. It works as a cleanup task in Maid, Janitor and Trove.
